The half turn about the central bond midpoint maps the dimer covering to itself. Rotation-paired positive coefficients with a unique maximum at that bond eliminate every nonidentity translation. The disjoint rank-one singlet constraints give a unique symmetric product of singlets and a uniform positive triplet gap, so this is a valid counterexample to the unqualified claim.

In the specified two-flux construction, moving the cut is implemented by the region product of onsite z half turns. Its commutator with the global x half turn is the product of the local spin parities; the exchanged pairs cancel and the fixed center gives minus one. The dressed half turn has scalar square and pairs opposite x eigenvalues at equal energy. The result applies to the twisted Hamiltonian, not to the untwisted spectrum.

Exchange of the two full matrix algebras makes the dressed half turn a swap composed with local unitaries, and its scalar square permits a change of local bases to a pure swap up to phase. For unitary B and C, the sum of B⊗C and C⊗B has norm two, ruling out the exact anticommutation in an independent-core model. This also rules out vanishing operator-norm errors to that model; for asymptotic algebra exchange with fixed finite core dimensions the stated compactness argument is valid.

The conclusion correctly separates the false rotation-only assertion from the conditional even-order rotation-center obstruction. The latter requires the nontrivial onsite spin parity at the fixed center and the stated defect-localization hypothesis for the SRE inference. It does not claim an untwisted gap closing or a literal substitution for translations in the conventional flux proof.

The half turn about (1/2,0) sends bond (m,y), with endpoints (2m,y) and (2m+1,y), to bond (-m,-y). A unique maximal coefficient at (0,0) rules out every nonzero translation. The disjoint triplet projectors have a unique singlet product ground state and a uniform gap at least the positive lower bound on their coefficients. This is a counterexample to the unrestricted rotation-only assertion.

For the stated order-two adjoint twist and cut geometry, both rotation and conjugation by G_A move the cut from gamma to R gamma; G_A squared is scalar. The global X half turn remains a symmetry because the local X and Z adjoint actions commute. In the dressed commutator the spin-parity signs cancel on off-center pairs, leaving -1 from the center. Thus the dressed half turn takes each simultaneous energy and X eigenvector to an orthogonal partner in the twisted sector.

The conclusion distinguishes the false unrestricted assertion from the conditional even-order rotation-center no-go. With localized independent core factors the dressed half turn is a swap up to local changes of basis and phase, using its scalar square. For B tensor C the anticommutation residual under swap has norm exactly 2, excluding even vanishing operator-norm errors in the localized swap/product description (or one can take a fixed-finite-dimensional limit). The SRE implication remains conditional on the stated defect-localization hypothesis; exact twisted-sector pairing alone proves no untwisted gap closing.
